text: The man's track beside the horse's, near Mapleton
why: ¶119 states that a man's track was visible beside the horse's, found close to Mapleton.

text: The man whose track joined the horse's near Mapleton
why: Refers only to the unidentified man whose track ran beside the horse's near Mapleton, as ¶119 describes. It names no one.

text: Thursday evening, picking up the tracks again close to Mapleton
why: ¶13 places the story on Thursday morning, and ¶117-119 take place later that day, with the sun setting, so Thursday evening fits. The tracks are picked up again near Mapleton.

text: When a man's track came beside the horse's near Mapleton
why: Restates ¶119: a man's track was visible beside the horse's near Mapleton.

text: Who was the man whose track joined the horse's near Mapleton?
why: A plain question that follows from the story's open thread about who the man beside the horse was. Its wording does not point to an answer.

text: Who was the man whose track joined the horse's near Mapleton? — the man who struck Straker down, following the horse
id: q.man_near_mapleton=the man who struck Straker down, following the horse
why: Asserts that the track-maker struck Straker down and was following the horse. The story only shows a man's track beside the horse's, not following it, and nothing so far establishes that this man is the killer.
